name: Execution Quality Check
description: The first month of standardized SEC Rule 605 execution-quality reports (August 2026), made comparable: venue-by-venue spread, price-improvement and execution statistics, plus a per-symbol explorer — exactly as filed, with hash receipts and documented data-quality notes.
data_source: Venue-published SEC Rule 605 amended-format reports for August 2026: Cboe BZX/BYX/EDGA/EDGX and IEX detailed 55-field pipe-delimited files + OES summary CSVs, fetched with SHA-256 receipts
records: 5 venues; 2,667,102 detailed rows; 13,299 symbols; 179 published summary rows; 73.1B executed shares (as filed)
detail: Venue comparison by order size band × stock universe × order type across the published statistics (price improvement, at-quote rate, effective/quoted spread, EFQ, realized spreads); per-symbol explorer comparing venues for any covered stock; coverage ledger of which publishers are live with probe evidence; method page with file receipts, normalizations, sanity filters and filing anomalies found during the build.
asymmetry: Brokers and venues benefit when execution quality stays fragmented across hundreds of separate monthly downloads; the standardized format exists so executions can be compared, but nobody has assembled the comparison. Investors comparing venues — or checking whether their fills are measurably worse than the market's — need the portage layer: many Download Sites → searchable, comparable tables.
pipeline_note: Header-driven parsing of the 55-field detailed files; EFQ unit normalization (verified ×100 on every Cboe row; IEX files verified schema-conformant and used as filed); conservative row-sanity filters for weighted statistics only (exclusions counted per venue, 2-10% of executed volume on Cboe, ~0.01% on IEX); notional fields excluded due to sentinel-value anomalies found in the first filings; 2026-09-25 refresh build (IEX added — published 2026-09-25) with Playwright browser smoke over the staged site; static, no backend.
